description.value: This study examined whether distinct ventral and dorsal anterior insula resting-state connectivity networks are associated with baseline craving and smoking cue reactivity in nicotine-dependent individuals.

spans.text: Whether vAI/dAI network connectivity differentially reflects internally generated craving and externally triggered smoking cue reactivity was tested.

value: we hypothesize that the vAI is involved in internally generated craving, whereas the dAI has a role in reactivity to external smoking cues.

description.value: Resting-state and task-based fMRI data were preprocessed with FMRIB Software Library tools, including MCFLIRT motion correction, BET brain extraction, slice-time correction, 6-mm FWHM Gaussian spatial smoothing, and high-pass filtering at 0.01 Hz. Spikefix identified motion and intensity spikes; task spikes were removed and represented with single-point confound regressors. Resting-state data were denoised using MELODIC independent-component analysis, with visually identified noise components regressed out to generate denoised time series.
